lesson_title: Four Times Thirty-Seven Times Twenty-Five, In Two Seconds
hook_text: No calculator. 4 × 37 × 25. Most people start at the wrong end.
clip_script: The anchor calculation. Four times thirty-seven times twenty-five. Worked left to right it is ugly: four times thirty-seven is one hundred and forty-eight, and one hundred and forty-eight times twenty-five is a long multiplication. Instead, apply the commutative law to swap thirty-seven and twenty-five, then the associative law to group four with twenty-five. Four times twenty-five is one hundred. One hundred times thirty-seven is three thousand seven hundred. Two laws, two seconds, and the answer is 3 700. In the examination you write the law beside each step: commutative, then associative. That annotation is the method mark.
visual_style: Three number tiles on a dark board; 37 and 25 slide past each other, 4 and 25 snap together into a glowing 100, then 3 700 stamps down in green with the two law names appearing as margin notes.
pacing: Slow ugly start, then two quick snaps and an instant answer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn all three laws by name.
